author: RollyJoger
quote: I have a hard time finding any games that come close in comparison. Everything in this game is intentional. Each characters is hand made and carefully thought out. I remember as a kid searching for interactions that would have some secret or something special. Even now as I go back and play it I always find something new that surprises me. I actually play it so infrequently because it’s one I want to keep being special each time I come around to playing it.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)

author: RollyJoger
quote: The story falls very short, while bringing characters like Niko back seem like a great choice, it’s brought in as a buffer for how bland the rest of the game is. The characters are not nearly as lovable as previous releases. Jason gives everything for Lucia and gets the bad ending of the stick the entire time. Even in the good ending it’s still a bad ending for Jason. I’ve never felt so restricted by a GTA game. I understand certain changes for the sake of realism but other things are purely gameplay. Ive never been in favor of intentionally restricting what a player can do in a game  like this but disincentivize it by an actual gameplay mechanic. In the mission where you come across the protestors it would only make sense that you could hit them and get a “Mission Failed” error like you would in GTA V. There is a perceived freedom in this game but it’s never left me more limited. Probably my least favorite installment in the franchise and I started playing with San Andreas on my PS2. It’s lost its soul and it’s sad to see.
